blockers.evidence: Official subprocess-local eagerly imports node-pty and its Windows inspector module imports koffi. The frozen Koffi 3.1.6 is post-statx-fix and has Android/Termux source-build evidence, but official support still excludes Android. node-pty v1.2.0-beta.15 has no Android support declaration; the Community NDK path must prove the unmodified package can build/load.
Official package declares sharp as a runtime dependency. sharp 0.35.x publishes platform optional binaries for desktop/server targets but no Android target.
blockers.nextProbe: Verify an exact sharp 0.35.4-compatible WASM fallback in the frozen Android runtime before changing status.

blockers.evidence: Official sandbox-local PLATFORM_CHAINS defines linux, darwin, and win32 only; an unlisted platform fails closed when confinement is requested. The package also imports Landlock and Windows ACL backends.
blockers.nextProbe: Provide an Android-safe runner through the official sandbox seam or wait for upstream Android support; then test under the APK app UID.

blockers.evidence: Official DSH tool-fs-search depends on @vscode/ripgrep; the ripgrep package resolves packaged binaries by process.platform/process.arch and exposes no Android target in the audited surface.
blockers.nextProbe: Package and verify an Android rg binary without relying on Termux system packages, or wait for upstream support.

conclusion: Node 22 is necessary but insufficient. The published top-level @deepseek-ai/dsh package eagerly carries the native closure, so profile-only row disabling cannot make the current official CLI package Android-safe.
